base.$description: Primary light surface. Default background for all light-mode screens.

sunken.$description: Recessed surface. Used for input fields, code blocks, and content wells that sit below the base.

raised.$description: Elevated card surface. Semantically distinct from base — conveys elevation even when the hex value matches.

inverse.$description: Dark surface. Used for tooltips, toasts, and elements that need to contrast sharply against light surfaces.

primary.$description: Primary text. Headlines, body copy, row labels. 19.6:1 on white — AAA.

secondary.$description: Secondary / supporting text. Subtitles, metadata, captions. 3.9:1 on white — passes AA for large text only.

disabled.$description: Disabled-state text. Non-interactive labels and placeholders. Below AA threshold by design.

accent.$description: Accent text. Links, highlights, active tab labels. MUST use green.700 (#7D9220) not green.500 (#C6FF2D) — green.700 achieves 4.6:1 on white (WCAG AA). green.500 achieves only 1.36:1 (fails).

onInverse.$description: Text on inverse (dark) surfaces. Tooltips, toasts, dark cards.

primary.$description: Primary CTA background. Electric Green (#C6FF2D). Background-only on light surfaces — never use as text color. Always pair with action.primary.fg.

fg.$description: Foreground on Electric Green background. Always Volt Black. 15.4:1 against green.500 — AAA.

secondary.$description: Secondary CTA background. Volt Black. Used for non-primary actions that need high contrast.

fg.$description: Foreground on secondary (Volt Black) background. White. 19.6:1 — AAA.

subtle.$description: Subtle dividers and non-interactive borders. Row separators, section edges.

strong.$description: Prominent borders. Selected states, focused inputs with dark outline, card stroke on light backgrounds.

focus.$description: Focus ring color. Electric Green outline on focused interactive elements. Used as a stroke, not a fill.

live.$description: Live-status indicator. Electric Green dot or badge. Always paired with a text label — never used as sole state indicator.
